name: 4B- (Stan Weinstein)

card.context: A stock late in a long Stage 4 decline (at least 30% under its 52-week high, under a falling 30-week line at the low) that has stopped making new lows, with its group turning and the market Green or Yellow. Version H, the one we trade: price is already back above the 200-day.
card.pattern: A cycle low with no close under it since, a higher low at least 3% above it set 10 or more sessions later on drying down-day volume, then a reclaim of a flattening 50-day and a pause of 2 or more closes above it, with at least 3R of room to the next ceiling.
card.trigger: PREV DAY HIGH BREAK: price trades above the highest high of the pause above the 50-day (with a two-session pause, the prior day's high), bought at market, no more than 4% past it.
card.stop: A few cents under the pause low when that is inside the owner's maximum, else under the trigger day's low or the prior day's low; the widest allowed (3%, 5% or 8%) is his call.
card.failure_mode: Stage 4 resumes: the break of the pause high stalls under the falling 150 or 200-day and the stop is hit, or a V bottom fails twice before it goes (META 2020). Bulkowski's own Stage 4 buys made money 24% of the time.

lookalikes.tell: Check the 30-week line at the low. A Remount takes back a flat or rising line that was lost for 5 or more closes on a stock still in an uptrend; a 4B- reclaims the 50-day after a 30% or more Stage 4 decline under a falling 30-week line. If the 150-day was rising when the low was set, it is a Remount or a pullback, not a 4B-.

Count the sessions since the low. A U&R buys the reclaim of a named low within 3 sessions of its undercut; a 4B- never closes under its cycle low and waits 15 or more sessions for a higher low, a 50-day reclaim and a pause before the buy.

Look at where the 30-week line sits. RDDT 2025-11 bounced off a rising 30-week line above its 200-day: a pullback in an uptrend, not a 4B-. A 4B- needs the 150-day falling at the cycle low and the low at least 30% under the 52-week high.

Time the entry. A capitulation buys the snap back within 3 sessions of a 2x-volume flush under every fast average; a 4B- waits weeks after the low for a higher low on drying volume and a 50-day reclaim, and it is not B26's parabolic exception.

Before entry: a report within 3 sessions, wait (w4b.earnings_window).

After entry: a close under the 50-day is a warning unless the 50-day is the chosen stop line (w4b.close_under_50_after).
mistakes: Buying plain 4B, a stock still falling, because it seems cheap. GTA: Much too soon to consider buying. TraderLion: do not catch the bottom.
Buying too early: a small base following a large Stage 4 decline, price still under declining moving averages (stageanalysis.net).
No higher low. Deepvue calls the higher low critical.
Treating a short-term trade as an investment, and holding it back down into Stage 4 (take the oath never to hold Stage 4).
Adding to it on the way up (A5 forbids it).
Ignoring overhead supply: buying right under the falling 30-week or 200-day line with less than 3R of room.
Chasing the reclaim day after an earnings gap (C28, C29), or buying the reclaim in the days before a report (B22), as Deepvue's NFLX example did.
Buying against the market or a weak group (forest to the trees).
Mixing up labels: a 4B- is not yet a Stage 1 base, although our app's stage code already calls it Stage 1.

short_mirror.note: None for our course (dossier 8.6). The mirror is a late Stage 2 stock that has lost its 10-week line (stageanalysis.net's 2B-, Weinstein's 3A, where the GTA tells holders to protect holdings with a close stop, not to short). Such a stock is nearly always above a rising 200-day, which B26 forbids shorting, so D47's reversed rule gives no usable short here. The stage short that is ours lives in the Stage 4A breakdown and the Bear gap, and in the owner's own words (2026-11-08): I will gladly short stage 4 downtrends as they reject the 200SMA from below (the 200-day rejection, setup 13's mirror).

best_conditions: After a broad market decline, once the market itself is turning back up (Deepvue: after most stocks have been downtrending); market reading Green, or Yellow at smaller size; after a correction, start with a few positions (F68). The group is basing too and the stock is among the first in it to reclaim its 50-day. A fresh reason for the turn helps, provided the buy is not in the 3 sessions before the report.

examples.limits: The hit count is high because the rule fires on most 50-day-pause breakouts after any 30% decline; the ten were picked from the 5R winners by eye, so they say what a textbook one looks like, not how often it comes. No group or market reading; prices split-adjusted by the vendor; SNPS and FDX predate the earnings table. The 26-of-39-weeks time option was not tested. Two named examples (NFLX, DXCM) are not a test of the edge. Nothing here is a published statistic, and none exists for the 4B- itself.

near_misses.why: close -10.2% under the 200-day on the day before the trigger; the house version (H) needs the close above it (B26). Weinstein's own version (W): a 50% decline, a 12% higher low and a 50-day reclaim with the close still 10% under the 200-day.

at the cycle low the 150-day was rising (528.74 against 521.41 20 sessions earlier). A 34% drop under a 150-day that was still rising at the low: a pullback in an uptrend, so a Remount (13) or a pullback buy, not a Stage 4 turn.
cycle low 21% under the 52-week high; the rule needs 30%. A 21% dip and a 50-day reclaim on a stock whose 52-week high was never far away: a pullback inside a range, not a 4B-.

the scan found the pullback into the higher low too shallow: the 39.47 high before it was only 4.1% over the 37.92 higher low, where the scan needed 5%. But the rally before the higher low was 11.2% (35.50 on 2019-01-03 to 39.47 on 01-18), so as the criterion is written (a rally of 5% or more before it) this AAPL passes the gate. A V off the January 2019 low: the higher low (2019-01-23, 13 sessions after the low) sits 6.8% above the cycle low and followed an 11.2% rally, then a pullback of only 4.1%; the scan read that shallow pullback as one leg, not a base (corrected 2026-11-10 against the bars).

conflicts: A rating or a trade: in the 2005 GTA, 4B and 4B- are ratings and the buys come later in Stage 2 (often at the move into 2A); from 2024 Weinstein and TraderLion treat the 4B- as a trade for advanced, short-term traders, while TraderLion's own guide says always wait for a clear Stage 1 base and Deepvue's page says there is no reason to be long in Stage 4.

4B or 4B-: our journal tag says 4B, which Weinstein's legend calls much too soon to consider buying; the buy is 4B-. The rename to 4B- (Stan Weinstein) and the move from Bases and Breakouts to Reversals and Reclaims are D-016 (10:1, 10:7).

B26: a 4B- nearly always sits under a falling 200-day, and both named examples (NFLX 54% under, DXCM 30% under) fail it at the entry. The card teaches Version H (above the 200-day) as the trade and Weinstein's version as a reading skill (D-009); on the scan's fixed-stop test Version W did better (30.1% against 22.2% to 3R), which the owner should see before answering.

C31: after a long decline the RS rating is low; either the 4B- is a mean-reversion trade exempt from RS 80 (D-011's default) or it cannot pass. The card's RS-line test is the dossier's; DXCM fails it.

What counts as the decline: depth (sharp decline, no number) against time (stageanalysis.net's 39 weeks); a time rule drops both named examples. The card takes depth only, 30% (D-070). The 1% flattening test for the 50-day rejects the NFLX entry; D-070 makes it a cue.
The higher low: Deepvue calls it critical; stageanalysis.net's mechanical 4B- does not test one; Weinstein is not quoted on it. The card requires it.

Weekly or daily: classic Stage Analysis is weekly (the 30-week line); every modern 4B- source triggers on the daily 50-day. The card reads Stage 4 on the 150-day (the 30-week stand-in) and triggers on the daily.
Hold short or long: TraderLion and Deepvue a short-term play; Ameet Rai the first step of a ride into Stage 2, adding along the way. The house trims and A5 win (D-146, D-135).

The stop: no 4B- source gives one; GTA practice is usually two stops (a trading stop and a wider investing stop, mostly at x.99 or x.49) that run well past 3%; the owner's RDDT note uses the 50-day. The default line and the widest allowed (3%, 5%, 8%) are D-005; the scan's pause-low stop fitted only 104 of 2,016 hits within 5%.

The trigger: the owner's Kicker ruling (over the previous day's high, not the close) is borrowed by analogy; he has not ruled on the 4B-. D-003's default applies it to every daily setup; the GTA's close-above-a-level is the other option.

The entry trigger type: the card files the pause-high break under PREV DAY HIGH BREAK (a two-session pause makes it the prior day's high); a longer pause makes it a small BASE BREAKOUT. The owner may prefer that label.

Deepvue's NFLX example: the $189 entry on 2022-07-15 or 07-18 came one to two sessions before the report (after the close on 07-19), which B22 forbids, and the $250 came 18 to 19 sessions later, not a couple of weeks; most of the move was the earnings gap.

The app cannot see a 4B-: the stage code reads NFLX and DXCM as Stage 4 and then Stage 1 from price change alone (it never measures the 150-day's slope), and the screener's Weinstein Stage 4 flag drops them the day they reclaim the 50-day. No detector, no Model Book card, no TRADE_PLANS row, no unit in UNITS-method; whether to build a scanner is D-004 (10:9).
Five Stan Weinstein quotes in quotes.json and the Weinstein claims in golden_cross.py, death_cross.py and patterns.py could not be found in any source read; they stay out of the lesson until sourced.

Measured evidence: none for the 4B- itself. Bulkowski's own trades (his site carries an AI-training notice) made money in 24.4% of Stage 4 buys and 69.3% of Stage 1 buys; a 4B- sits on the line between them, so the burden of proof is on the setup. Only our own scan (2,016 hits) is quoted.

Sources: the 2005 GTA is a forum-posted copy of a paid newsletter (short quotes only); the two TraderLion videos could not be read beyond their descriptions; Weinstein's 1988 book was not read, and the A/B/+/- codes are not verified against it.
